subject: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default — request/response vs prompts/outputs
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@finserve.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Question on what Redwood stores by default (requests vs prompts vs outputs)

Hi Marcus —

We're doing an internal review of vendor data flows and had a few specific questions about Redwood's default capture/retention for hosted API customers. Could you confirm the following for hosted (not Dedicated/Private) accounts in the EU region: 

1) By default, how long are request payloads (raw requests/prompts) retained?
2) Are model outputs (generated text, token-level metadata) persisted by default, and if so for how long?
3) How are derived artifacts (embeddings, reranking indices) treated by default?
4) If we ask for deletion of a particular conversation, what is the end-to-end time to deletion (including backups/snapshots)?

I've attached a short example of a call we want to exclude from retention (sample_call.log). Thanks for the quick help — we have a compliance checkpoint next week.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Head of Platforms
FinServe Inc.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@finserve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on what Redwood stores by default (requests vs prompts vs outputs)

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, then detail below. I've also attached a one‑pager (redwood-default-retention-summary.pdf) for your legal/compliance team.

TL;DR (Hosted API, EU region):
- Request payloads (user prompts/inputs): retained for 7 days by default. This covers raw requests used for routing, abuse detection, and short-term debugging.
- Model outputs (generated responses & token metadata): not retained long-term by default; retained for 30 days if "retain-responses" is enabled by the customer for debugging; otherwise ephemeral (7 days for short-term troubleshooting traces).
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, vectors): retained for 90 days by default when created via the embeddings endpoint (these are considered derived artifacts and used for caching/efficiency).
- Aggregated telemetry/metrics (latency, error rates): 365 days for observability (no user content included).

Notes and caveats:
1) Dedicated and Private deployments: For Dedicated customers we can accept configurations where Redwood does not keep request/response bodies at all — telemetry can be reduced to aggregated metrics only. Private/on‑prem builds are fully under customer control.
2) Residency: For EU region customers, all stored artifacts by default are kept in EU-hosted storage. Backups/snapshots are also stored in-region unless you opt into cross-region replication.
3) Deletion flow (high level): customer requests via Data Deletion API or support ticket -> items soft-deleted within 48 hours -> primary storage purge begins and completes within 30 days -> backups/snapshots purged within 60 days (see below for more detail).

If it's helpful, Marissa/Karthik — can you add the official runbook wording for deletion SLA and backup retention?

--
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha@finserve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on what Redwood stores by default (requests vs prompts vs outputs)

Adding the operational/compliance detail Samantha requested. I'm pasting the key points from our deletion runbook so you have verbatim language for SOC/attestation reference.

Runbook excerpt (condensed):
- Soft deletion window: When a deletion request is accepted (Data Deletion API or ticket), the object(s) are marked for deletion and moved to a soft‑delete tier within 48 hours. During this time they are unavailable for normal access.
- Primary store purge: After soft delete, primary storage objects are purged. This purge completes within 30 calendar days for Hosted customers; for high-volume/complex queries we may parallelize but still adhere to the window.
- Backup & snapshot purges: Immutable backups and longer‑term snapshots are retained for disaster recovery for up to 60 calendar days before being removed. Customers may request expedited snapshot purges for regulated workloads; we evaluate these on a case‑by‑case basis and provide an attestation when completed.
- Audit artifact: We produce a deletion confirmation with timestamps and object identifiers once the process completes.

Important: The 30/60-day windows are maximums under normal operations. Typical effective deletion from primary stores is often under 7 days for small datasets, but we cannot guarantee faster than the windows above.

I also want to clarify the definitions we use (this helps avoid confusion in questionnaires):
- "Request/Prompt": any user-supplied input (user text, structured payloads) sent to the API.
- "Output/Response": the model-generated text, tokens, structured completions, and any model metadata returned.
- "Derived artifact": anything created from requests/outputs (embeddings, reranking indices, cached KV blobs).

Marissa — attaching the one‑pager and the SOC2 FAQ if you want to include additional legal phrasing.

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Privacy Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. Two quick follow-ups: 

1) Can you confirm whether the 60‑day backup retention applies to encrypted snapshots that are written to cold storage? Do you provide an attestation/certificate when snapshots are purged?
2) Is the Data Deletion API the recommended route for bulk deletion (we have 18k conversation IDs to remove) or should we open a ticket?

I've attached our SOC2 questionnaire excerpt that asks specifically about backups.

Best,
Samantha

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@finserve.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T12:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on what Redwood stores by default (requests vs prompts vs outputs)

Samantha — short answers and next steps: 

1) Backups/snapshots: Yes, the 60‑day window applies to encrypted backups written to cold storage by default. We can initiate an expedited purge of snapshots for regulated requests; that requires an approval flow and may take up to 14 extra days depending on region and legal review. When we complete the purge we provide an attestation PDF with snapshot IDs and timestamps.

2) Bulk deletion: Data Deletion API supports bulk operations and is the recommended route for programmatic deletion (we handle queueing and rate limits). For very large batches (>10k IDs) we usually pair the API call with a support ticket so our ops team can monitor progress and expedite snapshot purges. I'll open a ticket once you confirm the ID list and whether you want expedited snapshot removal.

Next steps: If you send the list (or a sample CSV) to our secure intake link, we'll kick off the Data Deletion API job and create HubSpot ticket FS-9876 to track. Expect an initial acceptance/soft-delete acknowledgement within 48 hours.

Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/data-deletion-api
Secure intake: https://files.redwood.ai/secure-upload/FS-9876

I'll attach the retention summary to the ticket and include the deletion attestation when complete.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
